title: A Bakery for the Summer Revisited
premise: Yara Blackwood inherited a vineyard drowning in debt and a family that treats her as a ledger entry, so when the annual Blackwood reunion looms, she hires Theo Marsh, a widowed baker passing through town, to pose as her partner for the weekend. What begins as a transaction deepens as Theo's warmth draws Yara's estranged half-siblings into a fragile found family, while her uncle's scheme to seize the vineyard exposes how far the family will go to protect its power. At the summer festival's closing night, Yara must publicly say the sentence she has rehearsed for a decade—that she never wanted to be her father's heir, only her own person—and choose Theo not as a prop but as a home.
about_author: Ivo Reyes is a former pastry chef who traded early mornings at a bakery in the Azores for late nights writing love stories about people who rebuild themselves from scraps. They believe the best romances begin as small lies and end as larger truths.

chapters.title: The Ledger and the Loaf
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Drowning in vineyard debts and her uncle's condescension, Yara meets Theo when his food truck stalls outside her gate and his sourdough becomes the first honest thing she's tasted in months. Beat: hunger for something real, disguised as a business transaction.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Yara offers Theo payment to pose as her partner at the reunion; Theo, needing funds for his late wife's memorial bench, negotiates terms over flour and wine. Beat: two guarded people mistaking a contract for safety.

chapters.title: Rehearsing the Sentence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Rehearsing their cover story in the empty tasting room, Theo glimpses Yara practicing a private sentence she refuses to explain. Beat: curiosity kindling where professionalism should be.

chapters.title: Arrivals at Blackwood House
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The reunion begins; her uncle Ambrose performs benevolence while quietly courting creditors, and Yara's half-siblings treat her as an outsider. Theo's easy charm disarms her youngest sister, Nell. Beat: the fake couple's first real victory.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo bakes the reunion dessert from Yara's late mother's recipe card, and the family's stunned gratitude cracks Yara's armor in public. A dance under the porch lights feels nothing like pretending. Beat: the lie stops costing nothing.

chapters.title: The Uncle's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara discovers Ambrose has been forging her signature on loan documents, positioning to take the vineyard when she inevitably fails. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve; power revealed as appetite.

chapters.title: What Nell Saw
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Twelve-year-old Nell, who idolizes Theo, accidentally learns the relationship is fake and feels betrayed, mirroring every adult lie she's watched this family tell. Beat: the found family's first fracture.

chapters.title: Rain on the Trellis
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Storm-bound in the cellar, Yara finally tells Theo the rehearsed sentence's origin: at her father's funeral she was handed the deed instead of condolences, and she's been rehearsing her refusal ever since. Beat: intimacy through confession, not touch.

chapters.title: The Almost
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A near-kiss in the vineyard rows is interrupted by Ambrose's lawyer arriving with buyout papers. Yara signs nothing but realizes Ambrose has turned her siblings against her with lies about her competence. Beat: isolation as a weapon.

chapters.title: Bread for the Enemy
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Against Yara's wishes, Theo brings bread to Ambrose, probing for weakness, and learns Ambrose's empire is itself mortgaged to a developer who wants Blackwood land. Beat: the corrupt are also cornered.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Falls Apart
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Ambrose exposes the fake relationship at a family dinner, framing Yara as a fraud who rented a man to deceive them. Nell's hurt resurfaces publicly. Beat: humiliation, and the contract's cold end.

chapters.title: The Bench by the Road
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo installs the memorial bench alone, realizing he came for money and stayed for a family he was never paid to join. He decides to leave before he does more damage. Beat: grief teaching him what he actually wants.

chapters.title: Empty Kitchen
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Theo's departure leaves the vineyard silent. Yara confronts how quickly she made him a home and then let the family's verdict evict him. Beat: loneliness chosen is the hardest kind.

chapters.title: Nell's Evidence
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell, snooping in Ambrose's study, photographs the forged signatures and the developer's contract, then chooses Yara—the outsider—over the uncle who raised her. Beat: the found family's first true act of loyalty.

chapters.title: Siblings, Reluctant
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Armed with Nell's photos, Yara confronts her half-brother Marcus, who admits he believed Ambrose out of fear, not loyalty. A wary alliance forms. Beat: power begins to shift toward the truth.

chapters.title: The Festival Opens
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo returns to town for the summer festival, telling himself it's closure. He witnesses Yara publicly refusing Ambrose's final offer on the festival stage, voice shaking but unbending. Beat: admiration rekindling into hope.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Spoken
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Before the festival crowd and her assembled family, Yara says the decade-rehearsed sentence: she never wanted to be her father's heir, only her own person—and she will save the vineyard as hers, not his legacy. Beat: catharsis; identity claimed out loud.

chapters.title: Ambrose Unmasked
chapters.summary: Marcus's and Nell's POV. The forged documents go to the family and the bank; Ambrose's own creditors abandon him when the developer deal collapses. He leaves Blackwood House diminished. Beat: power's corruption devouring its host.

chapters.title: Flour on Her Hands
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara finds Theo at his food truck and, instead of an apology, offers him a job, a kitchen, and a place in a family that now includes Nell, Marcus, and her. Beat: the proposal that isn't a contract.

chapters.title: The First Honest Date
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Their first real date is the festival's last night—no cover story, no audience, just wine, bad carnival games, and the terrifying freedom of being seen. Beat: joy without performance.

chapters.title: Harvest Promises
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. First harvest under Yara's ownership: the siblings work the rows together, Nell names the new bench, and Theo's bread sells out at the farm stand. Beat: found family becoming ordinary, which is the point.

chapters.title: A Bakery for the Summer
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo signs the lease to open a bakery on the vineyard's edge, and Yara writes a new sentence—not rehearsed, just true—and says it to him at dawn. Beat: love in the present tense, at last.
